clue.text: Number that I can see is wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are in the wrong order and must be put right

explanation.surface: Someone points at a number on a chart and says the one they can see is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure here but something that numbs, pronounced NUM-er.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that removes feeling is literally a thing that makes you numb, hence a numb-er.

clue.text: Flying off?

parts.note: surface reading: leaving by taking off into the air
setter's reading: 'off' means unwell, so feeling ill because of flying

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying off' suggests departing; read 'off' as poorly and it describes nausea caused by air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nauseous during a flight is the condition named, and 'off' is a casual word for unwell.

clue.text: Outlandish story in article

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, surrounded

parts.note: a story can be an untruth

explanation.surface: A newspaper article carries a far-fetched story.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outlandish is strange and foreign, which is the adjective sense of the answer.

clue.text: End of The Wash outing, dull

parts.note: a spin is a short trip out, usually in a car

explanation.surface: A dreary trip to the far end of The Wash, the large bay on England's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a big estuary on England's east coast, so the clue seems to be about geography; the definition is the final stage of a laundry cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing machine finishes its cycle by spinning the clothes fast to drive out water.

clue.text: More serious judge is restricting contest

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one word closes around the other

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling limiting a competition makes things graver.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy can mean grave or weighty, so the comparative means graver.

clue.text: Goes through poetry hosted by star cast

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown about, so the letters are scattered and reset
a guest hosted by someone is inside their home, so one piece sits within the other

explanation.surface: A celebrity reads poems while an ensemble moves through a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or through something.

clue.text: Old sailor in Austria's rock climbing

indicators.note: in a down light, climbing means reading from the bottom upwards
the letters are sitting inside the following words

parts.note: read the letters backwards across these words

explanation.surface: An old seaman takes up mountaineering on an Austrian crag.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate of the Barbary coast, a seafarer of former times.

clue.text: Scorsese perhaps beginning to imbibe cocktail

parts.note: Martin Scorsese, the film director, is an example of a Martin

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The film director starts drinking a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorsese perhaps' defines by example, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka and vermouth.

clue.text: Gospel music essentially full of goodness, you'll see!

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it within

parts.note: Mark's is one of the four Gospels
my word! is an exclamation like goodness!

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its central letter

explanation.surface: Gospel music, at its heart, is full of good things — you'll find out.
explanation.walkthrough: MARK plus S form MARKS, which goes around the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are warnings that the speaker's prediction will be proved right in time.

clue.text: Harry hit on answer for part of clue?

parts.note: to harry someone is to pester them
to ram is to strike hard

explanation.surface: Someone named Harry hits on an answer to a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means the first two pieces are placed after the answer's abbreviation. Harry looks like a name, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement of letters is a common element in cryptic clues, so it is one part of a clue.

clue.text: Maiden with Flower still pronounced great work of art

parts.note: M for maiden, the cricket over with no runs
an aster is a daisy-like flower

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so a word is matched by its sound

parts.note: stillness is peace, said the same as piece

explanation.surface: A painting of a girl beside a flower, a still life, is declared a great work.
explanation.walkthrough: M = maiden comes from cricket scoring, where a maiden over yields no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is an artist's finest creation, an outstanding piece of art.

clue.text: Reportedly drops rule

indicators.note: reported words are heard rather than read, so go by the sound

explanation.surface: A report that someone is dropping a regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of rule, or the verb to rule, is the meaning used.

clue.text: Ivy was red around paths in front of houses?

indicators.note: letters moved around are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Autumn ivy turned red all around the garden paths.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is the private track leading to a house, where a car is parked; the question mark marks a loose description.

clue.text: Oddly knew heat must go in May — take advantage of it?

indicators.note: something that goes in another is placed inside it
oddly means take the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Someone who knew the May heat was coming urges others to exploit it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the proverb 'make hay while the sun shines', with 'it' being the sunshine of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to exploit a favourable opportunity while it lasts, as farmers cut grass in sunny weather.

clue.text: Be holy and pure, awkwardly avoiding university's excess

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is clumsy and out of order
avoiding something means leaving it out

parts.note: the letters before the removal, ignoring 'and'
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Telling students to be holy and pure while shunning campus life seems overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one U from the fodder before rearranging; 'and' joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is exaggeration, an excess of statement beyond the truth.

clue.text: Coolness in park

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a restrained, aloof manner
second meaning: a protected area of land, like a nature preserve

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their cool while sitting in a park.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both emotional restraint and a tract of land set aside for wildlife.

clue.text: Dog with bone gets stroke

explanation.surface: A dog with a bone gets patted.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet is a slim racing dog breed resembling a small greyhound.

clue.text: One goes up to check black lines on a map

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: B for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone climbs up to inspect black lines drawn on a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Isobars are lines on a weather chart joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: From below, starts to lift up feeble tabby cat, being sensitive

indicators.note: in a down light, reading from below means reading upwards
the start of each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Gently lifting a weak tabby cat from underneath, showing care.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactful person is sensitive to others' feelings and careful not to offend.

clue.text: Flipping sandwich bar where you queue outside

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over end to end

parts.note: a sub is a long filled roll

explanation.surface: An exasperated customer queues outside a sandwich shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive but applies only to the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus stop is a roadside spot where people wait in line for a bus.

clue.text: Call bishop over about good sort who's needed for wedding

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another
turned over means read the other way

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person

explanation.surface: Phone the bishop about a decent person required for the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: A saint is the crossword's model good sort, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The groom's chief attendant is an essential role at a wedding ceremony.

clue.text: Snack free, so eat it

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order

explanation.surface: The snack costs nothing, so eat up.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a common British light snack.

clue.text: Places to secure bags when travelling far with crooks abroad

definitions.text: Places to secure bags when travelling

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Travellers abroad worry about where to keep luggage safe from thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Racks fixed on a car's top carry luggage on journeys.

clue.text: Pursue husband in court action

indicators.note: a thing placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone pursues their spouse through the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to run after or pursue.

clue.text: Bit weird in empty catacomb

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
an emptied word has its inside cleared, leaving only the ends

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd

explanation.surface: Something strange in a deserted underground tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a small fragment, a tiny bit.

clue.text: Marine mammal leaving quarantine

parts.note: a seal lives in the sea

explanation.surface: A sick seal is released after a stay in isolation.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine an area is to close it off so nobody enters or leaves.

clue.text: Second to free Canadian officer

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: A Canadian policeman has a moment to free someone.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British slang, as in 'half a mo', for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

clue.text: Suggesting buzzer for competition

parts.note: to spell can mean to signify, as in 'spells trouble'

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a buzzer for use in a quiz contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A spelling bee is a contest in which entrants spell words aloud.
